scope: Only the 22 supplied records and their 11 primary papers were reviewed.

records.scopeCorrection: Final Δ need not bound degrees during the stream. Polynomial postprocessing.
Fixed η∈(0,1). Main figure conservatively uses O(Δ): theorem suppresses integer/small-degree conventions. No guessed numerical palette ratio.

records.correctedBound: O(logΔ) passes; O(n log n) bits
records.scopeCorrection: The dynamic sparse-recovery extension preserves asymptotic space and passes. An initial degree pass removes advance knowledge of Δ.
Known Δ: O(n log n) bits. Parallel degree guesses preserve two passes when Δ is unknown, with logarithmic overhead.

records.correctedBound: O(logΔ loglogΔ) passes; O(n log²n) bits
records.scopeCorrection: Insertion streams. Log expressions denote asymptotic classes; bounded degree is handled trivially.
For each a≥1 and large n, space O(n log^a n) cannot guarantee fewer than exp(Δ^{1/(4a)}) colors at Δ=200 log^{a+1}n. Not an exp(Ω(Δ)) bound.
In particular K=O(Δ) requires Ω(nΔ) space. Õ(n) space forces K=Ω̃(Δ²); no numeric frontier from suppressed logarithms.

records.correctedBound: O(n log⁴n) working bits + Õ(nL) external random bits
records.scopeCorrection: Δ is the current degree; L bounds final degree and must be known. Choosing L=Δ for a fixed degree cap gives Õ(nΔ) external bits.
Random bits count toward memory. This accounting differs from the external-tape algorithms.

records.correctedBound: Õ(n) working bits + O(nΔ) external random bits
records.scopeCorrection: Fixed degree cap Δ. The semi-streaming claim excludes oracle randomness; it is not a total-memory Õ(n) guarantee.

records.correctedBound: Õ(nΔ^{1/3}) for O(Δ²); Õ(n√Δ) for O(Δ^{7/4})
records.scopeCorrection: Tradeoff O(Δ^{(5−3β)/2}) colors with Õ(nΔ^β) working space. Proof assumes Δ=Ω(log²n) and integer powers, with routine rounding. Only the two supplied β choices are plotted.

records.correctedBound: O(ε⁻¹n log n) words; one pass
records.palette: (1+ε)Δ for fixed ε and Δ=ω(log n); Δ+1 in the small-degree branch
records.scopeCorrection: The theorem’s palette calculation uses Δ=ω(log n); bounded/logarithmic degree is stored and greedily Δ+1-colored. Do not read fractional palettes literally for tiny Δ.

records.palette: Δ, or correctly report a Brooks obstruction
records.scopeCorrection: Connected components that are cliques or odd cycles are checked separately. Final graph coloring; each edge appears once.
Each edge appears once. This palette is not promised for arbitrary graphs.
The theorem uses (Δ+1)/2<c≤Δ, c=Δ−k. Displayed k=0,1 give Ω(n); the general family remains in the inspector.

records.palette: κ+O(εκ+1); κ+o(κ) in the growing-κ regime
records.scopeCorrection: Source states (1+O(ε))κ. Atlas retains +1 for integer/small-κ correctness: one-block case is greedily κ+1 colored; multi-block bound is κ+λ+ℓ. Set ε=1/log n for Õ(n) space; unknown κ handled by parallel guesses.
Even insertion-only and κ known in advance. Constant λ gives quadratic space; this is a different accuracy than the relative-slack upper.

records.palette: Each vertex chooses from its own final dᵥ+1 list
records.scopeCorrection: The final list of each vertex must arrive before any incident edge. Source space assumes ordinary bounded-size vertex/color encodings.

records.palette: Promise χ≤q versus χ>q^t, integers q,t≥2
records.scopeCorrection: Stored subgraphs may be solved by exhaustive computation. This is a space result, not a polynomial-time guarantee.

records.correctedBound: Ω(n²/(q⁵·4^{q⁴})) bits; Ω(n²) for fixed q
records.scopeCorrection: Integer q≥5 for a nonvacuous gap, q=o(log^{1/4}n). Theorem allows q≥3 but q≤4 gives an overlapping promise. Gap and success differ from the upper: not a matching q² frontier.
Integers q,t; display t≥2 and qt≤n to keep the promise nonoverlapping and nonvacuous. Exact chromatic computations may be exponential.
3≤q≤polylog n; integer t≥2, qt≤n in this view. Matches upper up to logarithms on the common multigraph contract, not necessarily on short simple-graph streams.

decisions: Two atlas routes: constructing colors and deciding a chromatic gap.
Categorical symbolic formulas avoid invented numeric exponents or palette constants.
Robust external random tape is excluded only where the source explicitly permits it; the lower applies even with free randomness.
The original degeneracy shorthand omits unavoidable integer slack. κ+O(εκ+1) is a conservative atlas convention derived from the one-block greedy case and the multi-block formula κ+λ+ℓ.
The 2018 near-Δ bound uses Δ=ω(log n) for fixed ε; the small-degree branch returns Δ+1.
The 2026 deterministic paper's refined (1+η)Δ theorem is retained in the inspector; main plot conservatively uses O(Δ), avoiding unverified tiny-degree rounding.
Beyond Brooks lower range corrected to k<(Δ−1)/2 by substituting c=Δ−k into Theorem 2.
General-turnstile decision uses χ≥qt and multigraphs; unbounded stream length/intermediate frequencies belong to the lower's model.
Random-order decision lower uses q²/4 and success ≥1−2^{−q⁴}/4. It is not a matching lower for the upper's q² gap.
presentationCaveats: No claim of exhaustive literature coverage.
No generic randomized Δ+1 streaming lower manufactured.
Brooks lower plotted at k=0,1 only; general formula remains inspectable.
